requirement:
Only current results whose captured source inputs match the current source
and whose build configurations are compatible contribute counts to saved
execution-coverage checks under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`. Results with changed
inputs are identified as stale; results of unknown compatibility are
identified as unavailable. Both are excluded from combined totals.

A filtered run preserves the provenance of unselected results under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`. It does not make those
results fresh when their recorded inputs no longer match. Their process
reports and matching captured source remain available until replacement or
removal of the build artifacts.
rationale:
The marked tests cover each obligation in `requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`.

**Fresh results contribute counts.**
- `book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[stale_or_unknown_records_publish_no_current_file_totals]` first checks a fresh record. The report passes and shows `code.rs: 2/2 (100.0%) — pass`.

**Changed source or build inputs make a result stale.**
- `execution_coverage.rs#mod[tests]/fn[source_and_build_inputs_invalidate_on_addition_removal_and_dirty_content]` tests `fresh()` directly. It covers these cases:
  - modified, added and removed source files;
  - changes to `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `rust-toolchain.toml`;
  - new files in watched directories and previously absent watched paths;
  - removal of the manifest and lock file.
  - Each change makes the result not fresh, and restoring it makes the result fresh again.
- `book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[cargo_launch_metadata_does_not_invalidate_but_caller_build_environment_does]` covers build environment compatibility.
  - `cargo run` launch metadata does not invalidate a result.
  - Changes to `CC`, `RUSTFLAGS`, `CARGO_PROFILE_*`, `CARGO_TARGET_*` and a fixture build input each make it stale.
- `tests/execution_coverage.rs#fn[real_build_captures_dependency_files_and_environment_for_read_only_freshness_checks]` runs a real build. It checks that `include_str!` data, `build.rs` and `rerun-if-changed` files, `Cargo.lock` and both environment inputs are captured. Changing any of them gives `stale coverage`, restoring them clears it, and no stored files change.

**Stale and unknown results are identified and excluded from combined totals.**
- In `stale_or_unknown_records_publish_no_current_file_totals`:
  - A stale record makes the check fail with `stale coverage`, and no `- code.rs:` totals or `100.0%` appear.
  - An unsupported schema (unknown compatibility) fails the check with the incomplete-store message, `cannot establish the current test set`. No totals appear.
- `book.rs#mod[tests]/fn[unreadable_history_cannot_reintroduce_an_older_success]` covers invalid metadata, missing captured source, unsupported schema and missing profile. In every case the check fails and no positive counts are combined, so an older success cannot return.
- `filtered_runs_union_latest_attempts_and_invalidate_with_saved_source` checks that a source change marks all records not fresh and gives `stale coverage`. It also checks that a result from a different build configuration is not in the selected current set.

**Filtered runs preserve unselected provenance.**
- `check.rs#mod[tests]/fn[focused_recollection_leaves_only_the_unselected_result_stale_with_its_original_sources]` re-collects one test after a source change.
  - The unselected result stays stale and is reported as `stale coverage`.
  - Its attempt id, run id and original captured source are unchanged.
  - The re-run test is fresh and holds the new source.
  - No totals are published.
- `stale_or_unknown_records_publish_no_current_file_totals` also asserts that the SQLite store and the retained `.profraw` still exist after the stale and unknown checks.

**Configuration compatibility.**
- The check that a result's configuration matches the active one is enforced in two places. `store.rs#impl[Store]/fn[snapshot]` rejects tests whose run configuration differs from the active one, and the check in `book.rs#fn[load_saved]` compares configurations.
- `store.rs#mod[tests]/fn[incompatible_builds_reset_every_test_but_empty_focused_runs_do_not]` tests that rule under `storage.configuration_reset` and `storage.replace`. This test is not marked for freshness.
- The freshness-marked tests above still check that a result from a different configuration drops out of the selected set.

I found no unmarked or unasserted obligation, and there are no acknowledgments to account for. Selection and replacement obligations belong to the cited `index.selection` and `storage.replace` requirements and are not reassessed here.

text: :::{req} index.freshness
Only current results whose captured source inputs match the current source
and whose build configurations are compatible contribute counts to saved
execution-coverage checks under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.selection`. Results with changed
inputs are identified as stale; results of unknown compatibility are
identified as unavailable. Both are excluded from combined totals.
A filtered run preserves the provenance of unselected results under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.replace`. It does not make those
results fresh when their recorded inputs no longer match. Their process
reports and matching captured source remain available until replacement or
removal of the build artifacts.
:::{req} index.selection
Saved execution-coverage checks read the current coverage set under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.storage.current` from SQLite. Each check
uses one coherent database snapshot of test identities, states, provenance,
and processed measurements, so a replacement or update cannot mix results
from different snapshots within the same check.
Checks do not search historical runs or use a separate report-selection
metadata cache. Current test identities, states, and provenance can be read
without loading their detailed measurements.
Only current results with complete, available measurements contribute to
coverage under {cite}`requirements.test-coverage.index.freshness`.
Pending, running, and unavailable entries are reported under
{cite}`requirements.test-coverage.check.measurement`. Checking does not build
or execute tests and never restores a superseded attempt.
:::{req} storage.replace
After preparation and selection discovery succeed, and before any selected
test starts, Habeas atomically establishes the new coverage set:
- An unfiltered workspace invocation clears the entire previous set,
including results for tests that no longer exist. This includes
`habeas coverage` with no supplied arguments and `habeas test`.
- An invocation with an explicit package or binary restriction, test filter,
partition, or ignored-only selection is filtered. It clears results for all
selected test identities and preserves unselected results within the
active build configuration.
- Every selected test receives a pending entry without measurements.
Native default filters and the default handling of ignored tests still apply
to an unfiltered workspace invocation. `--run-ignored all` alone does not make
a workspace invocation filtered.
A selected test that never starts because of fail-fast, interruption, or
execution startup failure remains unavailable. Its previous result does not
become available again. A filtered selection containing no tests leaves the
current results and active configuration unchanged; an empty unfiltered
workspace selection clears the previous set.
If the atomic replacement cannot be committed, the command reports the
failure and starts no tests. The previously committed coverage set and active
configuration remain unchanged.
